name: Question 11
problem:
The $2$nd term of a geometric sequence with a positive common ratio is $\frac{3}{2}$, and the $4$th term is $\frac{2}{3}.$ Given that all terms of the sequence are positive, what is the first term of this sequence to be less than
$0.000\,11?$
worked_solution:
Since we are given that ${a}_{2}=\frac{3}{2}$ and ${a}_{4}=\frac{2}{3}$, we can find the common ratio $r$ of the sequence, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{n-m} & =\frac{{a}_{n}}{{a}_{m}} \\ {r}^{4-2} & =\frac{{a}_{4}}{{a}_{2}} \\ {r}^{2} & =\frac{\frac{2}{3}}{\frac{3}{2}} \\ {r}^{2} & =\frac{4}{9} \\ r & =\pm \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the common ratio is positive, we take the positive value. Now, since ${a}_{4}=\frac{2}{3}$ and  $r=\frac{2}{3}$, we can use the $n$th term formula to solve for ${a}_{1}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\ {a}_{4} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {(\frac{2}{3})}^{4-1} \\ \frac{2}{3} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {(\frac{2}{3})}^{3} \\ {(\frac{3}{2})}^{2} & ={a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =\frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $n$th term of the geometric sequence is

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =\frac{9}{4}\cdot {(\frac{2}{3})}^{n-1} \\  & ={(\frac{3}{2})}^{2}\cdot {(\frac{3}{2})}^{1-n} \\  & ={(\frac{3}{2})}^{3-n}\end{aligned}
$$

We want the $n$th term to be less than $0.000\,11.$
Hence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{3}{2})}^{3-n} & <0.000\,11 \\ \operatorname{log}⁡{(\frac{3}{2})}^{3-n} & <\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,11) \\ (3-n)\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{3}{2}) & <\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,11) \\ 3-n & <\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,11)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{3}{2})} \\ -n & <\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,11)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{3}{2})}-3 \\ n & >3-\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,11)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{3}{2})}\end{aligned}
$$

Estimating the right-hand side using a calculator, we get:

$$
3-\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,11)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{3}{2})}≈25.480
$$

Therefore, the $26$th term is the first term of the sequence that is less than $0.000\,11.$

Question 11
?

The 2nd term of a geometric sequence with a positive common ratio is 32, and the 4th term is 23. Given that all terms of the sequence are positive, what is the first term of this sequence to be less than 0.00011?

a
the 25th term
b
the 28th term
c
the 24th term
d
the 26th term
e
the 27th term
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since we are given that a2=32 and a4=23, we can find the common ratio r of the sequence, as follows:

rn−m=anamr4−2=a4a2r2=2332r2=49r=±23

Given that the common ratio is positive, we take the positive value. Now, since a4=23 and r=23, we can use the nth term formula to solve for a1, as follows:

an=a1⋅rn−1a4=a1⋅(23)4−123=a1⋅(23)3(32)2=a1a1=94

So, the nth term of the geometric sequence is

an=a1⋅rn−1=94⋅(23)n−1=(32)2⋅(32)1−n=(32)3−n

We want the nth term to be less than 0.00011. Hence:

(32)3−n<0.00011log⁡(32)3−n<log⁡(0.00011)(3−n)log⁡(32)<log⁡(0.00011)3−n<log⁡(0.00011)log⁡(32)−n<log⁡(0.00011)log⁡(32)−3n>3−log⁡(0.00011)log⁡(32)

Estimating the right-hand side using a calculator, we get:

3−log⁡(0.00011)log⁡(32)≈25.480

Therefore, the 26th term is the first term of the sequence that is less than 0.00011.
